source: Invest Like the Best — Why the markets are pricing AI wrong: July 2026 AI/semis selloff, private inference cloud, old-GPU repricing, ~$700B Blackwell/Rubin credit gap
summary: Credit risk to the AI buildout is real but likely overstated given the operating cash flow acceleration thesis
summary_extended: Baker acknowledges that rising real yields, widening credit spreads, and Meta's poorly-priced bond offering (with CDS blowing out) represent a legitimate bear case for the AI infrastructure buildout — the one risk he takes most seriously. However, he argues this credit risk is likely overstated because it only becomes severely negative if debt is required to fund the buildout. His core counter-argument is that if the installed compute base reprices to spot rates, the resulting acceleration in operating cash flows could fund most or all of the AI capex internally, eliminating the need for external credit. Baker went 'really deep on credit' to pressure-test this bear case and concluded that the repricing of compute economics is the key variable that resolves the credit concern. The investment implication is that credit market stress is not a sufficient reason to exit AI infrastructure positions, provided one believes in the compute repricing thesis.
